intro: How NS&I's savings accounts and Bonds work, which are variable and which fixed, how access and tax differ between them, and how NS&I protects savings.
explanation:
## NS&I is backed by HM Treasury, which protects savings without an upper limit

National Savings and Investments (NS&I) is backed by HM Treasury, so the savings held with it are secure. It secures all of a saver's money, including the amounts above the level that most banks guarantee, which is covered on the [Deposit Protection](/uk/savings/savings-accounts/deposit-protection-fscs/) page.

## Variable-rate accounts can change, and NS&I sets the rate

Direct Saver and Income Bonds are easy access accounts. Money can be taken out with no notice and no penalty, and the interest is taxable. Direct Saver adds interest to the account once a year, while Income Bonds pays it out monthly to the saver's bank account. Both can be held jointly.

Because these rates are variable, NS&I may move them in either direction from time to time, whether prompted by a Bank Rate change or by shifts in what the wider savings market offers. NS&I contacts savers in advance if a rate is going to be lowered.

NS&I's cash ISA is the Direct ISA: the interest is tax-free, and applicants must be 18 or over and UK-resident for tax. It is easy access, but it is not a flexible ISA, so every deposit in the tax year counts towards the ISA allowance even if some of it is later withdrawn. NS&I has no stocks and shares ISA or Innovative Finance ISA.

The Junior ISA is a cash ISA for children under 18, also tax-free. A parent or guardian manages it until the child is 16, and nothing can be withdrawn until the child's 18th birthday, when it becomes an adult cash ISA. How the allowance works is covered on the [Junior ISA allowance](/uk/savings/isas/junior-isa-allowance/) page.

## Fixed-term Bonds lock in the rate and the money

British Savings Bonds is the umbrella name for two kinds of fixed-term Bond. Guaranteed Growth Bonds add the interest to the Bond, and it is taxable in the tax year the Bond matures. Guaranteed Income Bonds pay interest out monthly, taxable as it is received. Each is sold in terms of 1, 2, 3 and 5 years, and each term is a numbered Issue with its own fixed rate.

Green Savings Bonds are also fixed for a term, with interest taxable in the tax year the Bond matures, and the money raised is matched by HM Treasury with spending on green projects chosen by the Government.

For all of these Bonds, money cannot be taken out before the term ends, a Bond that has been bought cannot be topped up, and each Bond is a separate investment with its own maturity date. Applying for them and managing them is done online.

## Premium Bonds pay prizes, and most interest is taxable

Premium Bonds do not pay interest. They offer tax-free prizes through a monthly draw, which is covered on the [Premium Bonds](/uk/savings/nsandi/premium-bonds/) page. Interest from the accounts and Bonds above, apart from the ISAs, is paid without tax taken off and counts towards taxable income, though whether any tax is due depends on total interest and the saver's allowances, which are covered on the [Personal Savings Allowance](/uk/savings/savings-tax/personal-savings-allowance/) page.
